evidence: host/owner-host.lisp:5122-5125: `(carried (and (boundp-global 'fn-owner-record-octets state) (f-get-global 'fn-owner-record-octets state))) (octets (if (and (consp carried) (natp (cdr carried))) (cdr carried) 0)) (r (fn-orcp-reserve (fn-owner-credits state) octets))`. The comment at 5114-5116 says the estimate is 'of the committed record octets the owner carries, fn-owner-record-octets'. fn-owner-record-octets (1116-1126) is the entry that syncs fn-hist and advances the (K . SUM) cache. Here the raw global is read and the count K is never compared with fn-sf-records-count.
fix: Take fn-hist in fn-owner-orcp-capture and call fn-owner-record-octets (sync, then fn-hist-bytes-carried) so the estimate is over the current committed records. If that cannot be done, refuse by name when the cache's K differs from fn-sf-records-count.

reviewer: fn-owner-orcp-capture (owner-host.lisp:5122-5125) reads the raw 'fn-owner-record-octets (K . SUM) cache. It does not call fn-owner-record-octets (1116-1126), which runs fn-hist-sync and extends the cache over the records committed since. The cache advances only through the limit-use, prepare (1781, 1952) and similar entries, so it lags the commits since the last such call. The comment at 5114-5116 names fn-owner-record-octets, which the code does not do. The reservation can therefore be smaller than the history requires. The unbound case is mostly moot, because install sets the global (owner-host.lisp:560). Severity is low: the estimate is already a heuristic multiplier, and the lag is usually small.
scenario: The cache only advances when something calls fn-owner-record-octets: a POST prepare, a publication verdict, or a limit use. A POST's prepare queries it before the POST's own record commits, so the cache always lags at least the last committed batch. After a burst of consumer or identity commits, or bulk transit relays that go through other entries, the lag is larger. A reclaim then reserves credit for fewer octets than the history holds. fn-orcp-reserve admits a rebuild whose real allocation exceeds the reservation, and the credit ledger's 'never over-committed' property (fn-mca-read-span-keeps-funded) no longer covers the pass. When no profile was installed, the global is unbound, octets is 0, and the reserve is the minimum.
title: Reclaim credit estimate reads the unsynced record-octets cache, not the carried figure the comment names
